Matched against Haar-random networks on the same graph (C-HAAR) and a gapped h=1.5 pipeline (C-GAPPED).

VERDICT: OUTCOME 4: SMOOTH. Primary verdict SMOOTH (w interp 7.76 > 6). Not cut-like: seed-mean m_0.9 = 4.75/4.34 (< 6), and 4.55 vs C-HAAR 4.62 (needs +3). Not cone-like: m_half = 8.50. This was the pre-registered EXPECTED outcome.
key_findings: The optimized MERA's onset of recovery loss (m_0.9 ~ 4.5 sites of 17) is indistinguishable from Haar-random networks on the same graph (4.62). The registered cut-vs-random test finds no difference.
m_half = 8.50 in every network, optimized or random, as the v3 identity requires (m_L + m_R = 17 to 1e-2): confirms the devil's-advocate finding on registered data.
C-GAPPED (h=1.5) is also SMOOTH with seed means close to the critical primary (m_0.9 4.91/4.19, w 7.59): no sign that the recovery profile depends on criticality.
C-HAAR is marginal on the smooth threshold: w interp 6.06 vs grid-point w 6.00 (I6 flag). This does not affect the primary outcome.
exploratory_not_registered: Optimized networks (critical and gapped) have broader loss curves than Haar (w ~7.6-7.8 vs 6.06) and strong seed-dependent left/right asymmetry (|m_L - m_R| up to 1.90 sites in the primary group, 2.26 in C-GAPPED) where Haar's is <= 0.04. POST-HOC; no registered test; not evidence for anything. A registered follow-up would be needed to say anything.
claim_level: Level 2 (outcome 4). Per the kill conditions no geometric language ('geometry', 'wedge', 'emergent') is used. Whether 'C-HAAR differs' (which would make it Level 3 negative) has no registered test beyond m_0.9, and on m_0.9 it does not differ.
counterfactual_novelty: 4 outcomes were registered as genuinely possible; outcome 4 was the stated prior. Moderate information, low surprise.
what_would_change_this: A chi-8 run (G5) showing the onset moves by >= 2 sites; a larger chi where 1601.01694 predicts sharp minimal-cut behaviour; a registered test of the width/asymmetry difference.
